intro: County elections officials run California elections, under the Secretary of State. Counties mail a ballot to registered voters.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state, county, and local offices, plus any measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Ballots mailed; drop boxes open
dates.detail: Counties start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Secure ballot drop boxes open Oct. 5 or 6. You can return your ballot any time from now through Election Day.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: This is the last day to register, including online. After Oct. 19 you can still register and vote the same day at your county elections office or a voting location, up to and including Election Day.

src.label: California Secretary of State — Nov. 3, 2026 key dates
California Official Voter Information Guide — dates to remember

dates.label: Early in-person voting
dates.detail: Vote centers open Oct. 24 in Voter's Choice Act counties. Early voting sites across the state are open Saturday, Oct. 31. Sites and hours vary by county.

src.label: California Secretary of State — Nov. 3, 2026 key dates
California Official Voter Information Guide — dates to remember

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 8 pm. Drop off your ballot at any polling place or drop box in California by 8 pm. A mailed ballot must be postmarked by Nov. 3. Mail it at least 7 days early to be safe.

dates.label: Last day for mailed ballots to arrive
dates.detail: A mailed ballot postmarked by Election Day counts if your county gets it by this date.

src.label: California Official Voter Information Guide — dates to remember

id_rule.text: In most cases you don't need to show ID to vote in California. You may be asked for ID if you are voting for the first time after registering by mail and did not give a driver's license number, state ID number, or the last four digits of your Social Security number.
